title: AI leaders take competing safety and control proposals to the UN
friendlyTitle: AI companies ask countries to work together on safety
summary: AI executives urged the UN Security Council to support international cooperation on advanced-system risks, while governments remain divided over how much control is appropriate. The discussion included incident notification and the challenge of coordinating national and regional rules.
friendlySummary: AI leaders told the United Nations that countries should cooperate on serious AI risks. Governments still disagree about how strong the rules should be.
whyItMatters: Businesses operating across borders should expect fragmented AI obligations before any global framework settles. Keeping model inventories, incident records and auditable controls now will make later compliance less disruptive.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI rules will probably differ between countries for some time. Businesses should keep clear records of their AI systems and any problems they cause.
